intent.raw_query: Tokyo city break, $3000 for couple, food and tech culture, April 2026 from SFO

experiences.name: Tsukiji Outer Market Food Tour
experiences.description: Explore the bustling Tsukiji Outer Market, sampling fresh sushi, tamagoyaki, grilled seafood skewers, and matcha treats from legendary local vendors. Engage with vendors who have operated stalls for generations and experience the authentic culinary heartbeat of Tokyo.

experiences.name: Akihabara Tech and Anime District Deep Dive
experiences.description: Immerse yourself in Tokyo's iconic electric town, visiting multi-floor electronics shops, retro game arcades, maid cafes, and cutting-edge gadget stores. Discover the intersection of consumer tech, gaming culture, and otaku subculture that defines modern Japanese innovation.

experiences.name: Senso-ji Temple and Asakusa Cultural Walk
experiences.description: Visit Tokyo's oldest and most iconic Buddhist temple, Senso-ji, strolling through the Nakamise shopping street lined with traditional crafts and snacks. Witness morning prayers, explore the five-story pagoda, and absorb the Edo-period atmosphere of the surrounding Asakusa district.

experiences.name: Ramen Alley Tasting Experience in Shinjuku
experiences.description: Navigate the narrow, atmospheric lanes of Shinjuku's Omoide Yokocho (Memory Lane) and nearby ramen shops, tasting regional ramen styles from tonkotsu to miso. Join a guided tasting session or self-explore izakayas and ramen counters for an authentic after-dark Tokyo dining ritual.

experiences.name: teamLab Borderless Digital Art Museum
experiences.description: Experience one of the world's most celebrated digital art installations where technology and culture merge into breathtaking immersive environments. Walk through rooms of interactive light, sound, and projection art created by the pioneering art collective teamLab, blending Japanese aesthetics with futuristic innovation.

trip_options.title: Budget Explorer - Tokyo, Japan
trip_options.description: Save money without sacrificing the experience. Perfect for travelers who value authentic local experiences over luxury.

day_by_day.morning: No activities — flight in transit
day_by_day.afternoon: No activities — flight in transit
day_by_day.evening: Arrive at Narita/Haneda Airport at 22:30 on United Airlines flight UA. Clear immigration and customs, collect luggage, and purchase a Suica or Pasmo IC card at the airport for convenient public transport throughout the trip. Take the airport limousine bus or train to your hotel (Aegean Bliss Resort, Tokyo). Check in, freshen up, and rest.

meals.breakfast: On the plane
meals.lunch: On the plane
meals.dinner: Grab a quick and affordable bite at the airport convenience store (7-Eleven or FamilyMart) — try onigiri (rice balls), sandwiches, or instant ramen for under ¥500

day_by_day.notes: Keep Day 1 light — arrival is late at night. Confirm hotel check-in arrangements in advance since it is after 10 PM. Airport convenience stores are open 24/7 and offer surprisingly good, cheap food. Budget tip: Narita Express (N'EX) or Keikyu Line from Haneda are the most cost-effective rail options.

day_by_day.morning: Start slow after jet lag. After breakfast, head to Asakusa — Tokyo's most traditional neighborhood. Visit Senso-ji Temple (free entry), walk through Nakamise Shopping Street for souvenirs and snacks, and admire the iconic Kaminarimon Gate. Arrive early (before 9 AM) to beat the crowds.
day_by_day.afternoon: Explore the Asakusa area further — visit Asakusa Culture Tourist Information Center (free, great rooftop view of Senso-ji). Walk along the Sumida River and cross the Azuma Bridge. Then head to nearby Akihabara (Electric Town) — Tokyo's legendary tech and anime hub. Browse multi-floor electronics stores like Yodobashi Camera and quirky retro game shops.
day_by_day.evening: Spend the evening in Akihabara exploring themed cafes and neon-lit streets. Visit a maid cafe for a unique cultural experience (budget around ¥1,000–¥1,500 for entry + drink). Window-shop retro game stores and anime merchandise shops.

meals.breakfast: Hotel breakfast or nearby convenience store — onigiri, tamagoyaki, and canned coffee for under ¥500
meals.lunch: Asakusa Ramen at Asakusa Rairai-ken or a bowl of soba at a local standing noodle shop — budget ¥700–¥1,000
meals.dinner: Akihabara curry house or a gyudon (beef bowl) at Yoshinoya or Matsuya for ¥500–¥800

day_by_day.notes: April in Tokyo is cherry blossom season — check if sakura are still blooming along the Sumida River for stunning views. Wear comfortable walking shoes. Suica card makes transit seamless between Asakusa and Akihabara.

day_by_day.morning: Head to Shibuya — start at the famous Shibuya Crossing, one of the busiest intersections in the world. Visit the Hachiko Statue (iconic meeting spot). Walk up to Shibuya Sky observation deck (¥2,000) for panoramic city views, or save money with the free view from Shibuya Stream rooftop terrace.
day_by_day.afternoon: Explore Harajuku — walk down Takeshita Street for quirky youth fashion, crepes, and pop culture. Then stroll through the elegant Omotesando Avenue (Tokyo's Champs-Élysées). Visit Meiji Shrine (free entry) set in a peaceful forested area — a beautiful contrast to the city buzz.
day_by_day.evening: Return to Shibuya for dinner and evening atmosphere. Explore the underground Shibuya food halls (depachika) in Shibuya Hikarie or Shibuya 109 for affordable bento boxes and street food.

meals.breakfast: Convenience store breakfast or a morning set at a local kissaten (old-school Japanese coffee shop) — ¥400–¥700
meals.lunch: Crepes and takoyaki on Takeshita Street in Harajuku — ¥500–¥800
meals.dinner: Ramen at Ichiran Shibuya (personal booth dining experience) — ¥1,000–¥1,300

day_by_day.notes: Meiji Shrine is free but donations are welcome. Harajuku is best explored on weekends for full Harajuku fashion culture, but weekday visits are less crowded. April cherry blossoms may still be visible in Yoyogi Park adjacent to Meiji Shrine.

day_by_day.morning: Visit Shinjuku — start at Shinjuku Gyoen National Garden (¥500 entry), one of Tokyo's most beautiful parks, especially stunning during cherry blossom season. Spend 2–3 hours strolling through Japanese, French, and English garden sections.
day_by_day.afternoon: Explore Shinjuku's vibrant streets — visit Kabukicho (Tokyo's entertainment district) during the day for sightseeing. Head to the Tokyo Metropolitan Government Building for a FREE observation deck with sweeping city views (open until 10:30 PM on some days). Browse the discount electronics and camera shops in the West Shinjuku area.
day_by_day.evening: Experience Golden Gai — a famous maze of tiny alleyways with over 200 micro-bars, each seating only 5–8 people. Have a drink and chat with locals and travelers. Then walk through the neon-lit streets of East Shinjuku for a quintessential Tokyo nightlife experience.

meals.breakfast: Onigiri and green tea from 7-Eleven — ¥300–¥500
meals.lunch: Katsu curry at CoCo Ichibanya or tonkatsu teishoku (set meal) near Shinjuku — ¥800–¥1,200
meals.dinner: Yakitori skewers and draft beer at a standing izakaya near Golden Gai — ¥1,000–¥1,500

day_by_day.notes: Tokyo Metropolitan Government Building observation deck is completely FREE — one of the best budget views in Tokyo. Golden Gai bars may charge a small table/seating fee (¥300–¥500) but drinks are affordable. Shinjuku Gyoen does not allow alcohol, so save that for Golden Gai.

day_by_day.morning: Day trip to Odaiba — Tokyo's futuristic man-made island. Take the Yurikamome monorail (scenic ride over Rainbow Bridge) from Shimbashi Station. Visit teamLab Borderless or teamLab Planets (book tickets in advance, ¥3,200) — world-famous immersive digital art museum that perfectly blends tech and culture.
day_by_day.afternoon: After teamLab, explore Odaiba's free attractions — walk along the waterfront promenade with views of Rainbow Bridge and the Statue of Liberty replica. Visit DiverCity Tokyo Plaza to see the life-size RX-78 Gundam statue (free). Browse the Palette Town shopping complex or relax at Odaiba Seaside Park.
day_by_day.evening: Head back toward central Tokyo. Stop at Tsukiji Outer Market area for an evening stroll, or visit nearby Ginza for window shopping along Japan's most upscale shopping street (free to walk, no need to buy anything).

meals.breakfast: Hotel or convenience store — ¥300–¥500
meals.lunch: Food court inside DiverCity Tokyo Plaza or a ramen shop in Odaiba — ¥800–¥1,200
meals.dinner: Affordable sushi at a conveyor belt sushi (kaiten-zushi) restaurant like Sushiro or Kura Sushi near Ginza or your hotel — ¥1,000–¥1,500

day_by_day.notes: Book teamLab tickets well in advance as they sell out quickly. The Yurikamome monorail offers stunning views of Tokyo Bay — sit at the front for the best experience. Odaiba is very walkable once you arrive.

day_by_day.morning: Explore Ueno — visit Ueno Park (free), one of Tokyo's largest public parks and a major cherry blossom spot. Walk through the park and visit the Ueno Toshogu Shrine (free exterior). Browse the Tokyo National Museum (¥1,000) — Japan's largest museum with incredible cultural artifacts, samurai armor, and ancient art.
day_by_day.afternoon: Head to Yanaka — one of Tokyo's best-preserved old shitamachi (downtown) neighborhoods that survived WWII bombing. Walk through Yanaka Ginza shopping street, browse vintage shops and local craft stores, and soak in old Tokyo atmosphere. Visit Yanaka Cemetery (free, beautiful and peaceful).
day_by_day.evening: Return to Ueno for Ameyoko Market — a lively open-air market street with street food, fresh seafood, clothing, and discount goods. Great for people-watching and budget shopping.

meals.breakfast: Morning set at a local kissaten near the hotel — ¥500–¥700
meals.lunch: Menchi katsu (deep-fried meat cutlet) or croquettes from a Yanaka Ginza street stall — ¥200–¥400 per item
meals.dinner: Fresh seafood don (rice bowl) or grilled skewers at Ameyoko Market stalls — ¥800–¥1,200

day_by_day.notes: Ueno Park is free and beautiful in April. The Tokyo National Museum offers reduced admission on certain days — check their website. Yanaka is a photographer's dream with its traditional townscape, temples, and cats.

day_by_day.morning: Visit Akihabara again with more focus — dive deeper into the tech culture. Explore the multi-floor retro game shops (Super Potato is a must), visit Yodobashi Akiba (massive electronics megastore), and check out the latest gadgets, components, and robotics at specialty stores.
day_by_day.afternoon: Head to Kanda and Jimbocho — Tokyo's famous used bookstore district. Browse thousands of secondhand books, vintage manga, old maps, and antique prints. Even if you can't read Japanese, the atmosphere and visual culture are fascinating. Visit Kanda Myojin Shrine (free) — a beautiful shrine closely associated with Tokyo's tech and business culture.
day_by_day.evening: Evening in Ochanomizu or Akihabara — visit a Japanese arcade (game center) like SEGA or Taito Station. Try UFO catcher machines, rhythm games (Taiko no Tatsujin, Dance Dance Revolution), and fighting games for ¥100 per play.

meals.breakfast: Convenience store or hotel — ¥300–¥500
meals.lunch: Standing soba or udon noodle shop in Akihabara — ¥500–¥700
meals.dinner: Curry rice at a local curry chain (Coco Ichibanya or Go! Go! Curry!) — ¥700–¥1,000

day_by_day.notes: Kanda Myojin Shrine is particularly meaningful for tech culture — it's famous for IT and digital industry blessings, and many tech companies visit here. Arcade games are a great budget evening activity — ¥1,000 can last a long time.

day_by_day.morning: Day trip to Nikko (about 2 hours from Tokyo via Tobu Nikko Line — budget round trip ¥2,600–¥5,000 depending on train type). Visit the UNESCO World Heritage Toshogu Shrine complex — one of Japan's most ornately decorated shrines, set in ancient cedar forests.
day_by_day.afternoon: Continue exploring Nikko — walk to Rinno-ji Temple, Futarasan Shrine, and the famous Shinkyo Sacred Bridge (red lacquered bridge over the Daiya River). If time permits, take a short bus ride to Kegon Falls — one of Japan's most impressive waterfalls.
day_by_day.evening: Return to Tokyo by early evening. Rest and relax at the hotel or grab a simple dinner near the hotel.

meals.breakfast: Early convenience store breakfast before departure — ¥300–¥500
meals.lunch: Yuba (tofu skin) dishes — Nikko's local specialty — at a small restaurant near the shrines — ¥1,000–¥1,500
meals.dinner: Simple teishoku (set meal) at a local restaurant near your hotel or convenience store bento — ¥600–¥900

day_by_day.notes: Purchase a Tobu Nikko Pass for the best value on trains and local buses in Nikko. Entry to Toshogu Shrine area costs ¥1,300. Start early (depart by 7–8 AM) to maximize time in Nikko. April weather in Nikko can be cooler than Tokyo — bring a light jacket.

day_by_day.morning: Explore Roppongi — visit the Mori Art Museum (¥2,000) atop Roppongi Hills Mori Tower, which also includes the Tokyo City View observation deck. The museum focuses on contemporary art and often features cutting-edge tech-art exhibitions. The observation deck offers stunning 360-degree views.
day_by_day.afternoon: Walk to Azabu-Juban — a charming, upscale-yet-approachable neighborhood near Roppongi. Stroll the local shopping streets and visit the small Azabu-Juban Onsen (public hot spring bath, ¥1,500) for a traditional Japanese bathing experience. Then head to Minato area — walk along the waterfront near Hamamatsucho.
day_by_day.evening: Visit the teamLab Borderless or explore the free light installations around Roppongi Art Night (check if any art events are happening in April). Alternatively, enjoy the Roppongi evening atmosphere with budget izakaya dining.

meals.breakfast: Hotel breakfast or nearby bakery — ¥400–¥700
meals.lunch: Affordable lunch set at a local Roppongi restaurant — many offer ¥800–¥1,200 lunch specials
meals.dinner: Izakaya dinner in Roppongi or Azabu-Juban — order edamame, karaage chicken, and draft beer — ¥1,200–¥1,800

day_by_day.notes: Roppongi is known for nightlife but is equally interesting during the day for its world-class art scene. The Mori Art Museum combined ticket with Tokyo City View is great value. Azabu-Juban Onsen is a hidden gem — a natural hot spring in the middle of Tokyo.

day_by_day.morning: Visit Tsukiji Outer Market early morning (best before 10 AM) — browse fresh seafood stalls, buy tamagoyaki (rolled egg), fresh uni (sea urchin), and sample street food. The outer market is free to walk through. Then head to nearby Hamarikyu Gardens (¥300) — a beautiful traditional Japanese garden with a tidal pond, right next to the skyscrapers.
day_by_day.afternoon: Take a water bus from Hamarikyu to Asakusa (¥1,040) — a scenic river cruise along the Sumida River passing under 12 bridges. Arrive in Asakusa and revisit any spots you missed on Day 2, or explore the backstreets of Kappabashi (Kitchen Town) — a street full of professional cooking equipment, plastic food models, and kitchen goods.
day_by_day.evening: Spend the evening in Asakusa — enjoy the beautifully lit Senso-ji Temple at night (stunning and far less crowded than daytime). Browse the evening street food vendors.

meals.breakfast: Fresh seafood breakfast at Tsukiji Outer Market — fresh sushi, tamago, and scallops on a stick — ¥800–¥1,500
meals.lunch: Bento box from a depachika (department store basement food hall) near Ginza — ¥600–¥1,000
meals.dinner: Tempura teishoku at a local Asakusa restaurant — ¥900–¥1,300

day_by_day.notes: Tsukiji Outer Market is still very active even though the inner wholesale market moved to Toyosu. The water bus from Hamarikyu to Asakusa is a scenic and affordable way to see Tokyo from the water. Senso-ji at night is magical and much less crowded.

day_by_day.morning: Explore Shimokitazawa — Tokyo's coolest bohemian neighborhood, known for vintage clothing stores, indie music venues, theater culture, and a laid-back creative vibe. Browse the dozens of secondhand and vintage clothing shops (many items ¥500–¥2,000). Visit local record stores and indie bookshops.
day_by_day.afternoon: Head to Nakameguro — walk along the Meguro River canal, lined with boutique cafes, art galleries, and independent shops. This area is especially beautiful during cherry blossom season (petals may still be falling in mid-April). Visit a specialty coffee roaster for a quality pour-over coffee (¥500–¥700).
day_by_day.evening: Return to Shibuya or Shinjuku for a final big-city evening experience. Visit a rooftop bar for one drink with a view, or explore the underground izakaya alleys of Memory Lane (Omoide Yokocho) in Shinjuku for smoky yakitori skewers.

meals.breakfast: Local kissaten (retro coffee shop) in Shimokitazawa — morning set with toast, egg, and coffee — ¥500–¥700
meals.lunch: Curry or pasta at a cozy Shimokitazawa cafe — ¥800–¥1,100
meals.dinner: Yakitori and cold beer at Omoide Yokocho (Memory Lane) in Shinjuku — ¥1,000–¥1,500

day_by_day.notes: Shimokitazawa is a must for culture lovers — it represents a very different, alternative side of Tokyo away from the tourist trail. Nakameguro is Instagram-famous but genuinely beautiful in person. Memory Lane in Shinjuku is tiny, smoky, and utterly authentic — a true Tokyo experience.

day_by_day.morning: Visit the National Museum of Emerging Science and Innovation (Miraikan) on Odaiba (¥630) — Japan's premier science and technology museum. See ASIMO the Honda robot, interactive AI and robotics exhibits, a giant globe display showing real-time Earth data, and space exploration exhibits. Perfect for tech culture enthusiasts.
day_by_day.afternoon: Head to Shiodome and Shimbashi — visit the Panasonic Center Tokyo (free) for interactive tech and smart home displays. Walk through the Caretta Shiodome shopping complex and enjoy the free sky-high views from its upper floors. Then visit the historic Shimbashi area — the site of Japan's first railway station.
day_by_day.evening: Final big evening out — head to a Tokyo Tower visit (¥1,200 for main deck) for nighttime illumination views, or opt for the free view from the Tokyo Metropolitan Government Building in Shinjuku. Celebrate your last full evening with a proper sit-down Japanese dinner.

meals.breakfast: Hotel breakfast or convenience store — ¥300–¥500
meals.lunch: Food court at Caretta Shiodome or nearby ramen shop — ¥700–¥1,000
meals.dinner: Celebratory dinner at a mid-range Japanese restaurant — try shabu-shabu or sukiyaki hot pot — ¥1,500–¥2,500 (splurge night!)

day_by_day.notes: Miraikan is one of the most underrated museums in Tokyo for tech lovers — highly recommended. Book the ASIMO robot demonstration show times in advance on their website. Tokyo Tower is best seen illuminated at night — the red and white structure is iconic and beautiful.

day_by_day.morning: Final morning in Tokyo — wake up early for one last convenience store breakfast or a quick bowl of ramen. Do any last-minute souvenir shopping at a nearby Don Quijote (discount variety store open 24 hours) or a 100-yen shop (Daiso or Seria) for affordable gifts. Pack and check out of the hotel.
day_by_day.afternoon: Head to the airport with plenty of time — allow at least 2–3 hours before your flight for check-in, immigration, and security. If time permits before leaving for the airport, visit the hotel neighborhood one last time for a final walk and photos. Use your remaining Suica card balance on transport and convenience store purchases (or get a refund at the airport).
day_by_day.evening: Departure. Browse duty-free shops at the airport for last-minute Japanese snacks, cosmetics, and whisky. Board your flight home with wonderful memories of Tokyo.

meals.breakfast: Final convenience store breakfast — onigiri, tamagoyaki, and canned matcha latte — ¥400–¥600
meals.lunch: Airport ramen or sushi restaurant inside the terminal — ¥1,000–¥1,500 (airport prices slightly higher)
meals.dinner: On the plane or airport food before boarding

day_by_day.notes: Return your Suica/Pasmo card at the airport service center for a ¥500 deposit refund (minus any remaining balance which is also refunded). Leave extra time for airport procedures. Don Quijote stores are open 24 hours and are excellent for last-minute affordable souvenirs — Japanese snacks, Kit Kat flavors, and cosmetics are popular choices.

trip_options.title: Classic Tokyo, Japan Experience
trip_options.description: The sweet spot between comfort and value. Enjoy quality accommodations, diverse experiences, and good food.

experiences.description: Explore the bustling Tsukiji Outer Market, sampling fresh sushi, tamagoyaki, grilled seafood skewers, and matcha treats from legendary local vendors. Engage with vendors who have operated stalls for generations and experience the authentic culinary heartbeat of Tokyo.

Join a guided tasting session or self-explore izakayas and ramen counters for an authentic after-dark Tokyo dining ritual.

day_by_day.morning: No activities scheduled — late-night arrival at 22:30
day_by_day.afternoon: No activities scheduled — late-night arrival at 22:30
day_by_day.evening: Arrive at Narita/Haneda Airport at 22:30 on Flight UA. Clear customs and immigration, collect luggage, and take the airport express train or limousine bus to your hotel (Aegean Bliss Resort, Tokyo). Check in, freshen up, and get settled. Pick up a Suica/Pasmo IC card at the airport for easy transit throughout your stay.

meals.breakfast: On the plane
meals.lunch: On the plane
meals.dinner: Grab a quick late-night bite at the airport — try a bowl of udon or soba from one of the 24-hour airport eateries, or pick up an onigiri and snacks from a convenience store (7-Eleven or FamilyMart) near the hotel (¥500–¥1,000)

day_by_day.notes: Keep Day 1 light. Jet lag will be significant. Prioritize rest so you're energized for the full days ahead. Confirm hotel check-in details in advance as you'll arrive late. Tokyo convenience stores (konbini) are excellent for late-night snacks and essentials.

day_by_day.morning: Sleep in and recover from jet lag. After a slow start, head to a nearby neighborhood café for breakfast. Take a leisurely walk around your hotel's local area to get oriented — explore nearby streets, a local shrine, or a neighborhood park to gently ease into Tokyo life.
day_by_day.afternoon: Head to Senso-ji Temple and Asakusa Cultural Walk. Visit Tokyo's oldest and most iconic Buddhist temple, stroll through the iconic Kaminarimon (Thunder Gate), walk the Nakamise shopping street browsing traditional crafts, snacks, and souvenirs. Explore the surrounding Asakusa neighborhood, including Asakusa Shrine and the rickshaw-lined streets.
day_by_day.evening: Stay in Asakusa for dinner and evening atmosphere. Walk along the Sumida River for views of Tokyo Skytree illuminated at night. Enjoy a relaxed evening stroll before heading back to the hotel.

meals.breakfast: Local neighborhood café or hotel breakfast — try a Japanese morning set (tamago gohan, miso soup, grilled fish) at a nearby kissaten (¥600–¥1,200)
meals.lunch: Grab street food along Nakamise-dori in Asakusa — try ningyo-yaki (small cakes), melonpan, or a sit-down meal at a local tempura teishoku restaurant (¥900–¥1,500)
meals.dinner: Dine at a mid-range izakaya in Asakusa — order yakitori, edamame, karaage, and cold Asahi draft beer. Try Sometaro for savory okonomiyaki (¥2,000–¥3,500 per person)

day_by_day.notes: April in Tokyo is cherry blossom season — check if Ueno Park (a short walk from Asakusa) still has blooms. Senso-ji is open 24/7 but most shops open around 10:00. Wear comfortable walking shoes.

day_by_day.morning: Start early with the Tsukiji Outer Market Food Tour. Arrive by 8:00–9:00 AM to beat the crowds. Sample fresh sushi, tamagoyaki (rolled egg omelet), grilled seafood skewers, fresh oysters, and tuna-topped rice bowls from the market stalls. This is one of Tokyo's best food experiences — take your time grazing through the stalls.
day_by_day.afternoon: After Tsukiji, walk or take the subway to Ginza — Tokyo's upscale shopping and cultural district. Browse the flagship stores, visit the free observation decks at Itoya (the iconic stationery store), and explore the Ginza Six complex. Pop into the free Pola Museum Annex or any gallery for a cultural interlude.
day_by_day.evening: Head to Shiodome or Shimbashi for dinner, or return toward your hotel neighborhood. Explore a local izakaya or try a standing sushi bar (tachinomi) for a more casual, affordable evening.

meals.breakfast: Tsukiji Outer Market — graze on fresh sushi breakfast, tamagoyaki, and grilled scallops. Budget ¥1,500–¥2,500 for a full market breakfast crawl
meals.lunch: Light lunch in Ginza — try a department store basement (depachika) bento or a ramen shop near Shimbashi station (¥900–¥1,400)
meals.dinner: Standing sushi bar or mid-range sushi restaurant near Ginza or your hotel area — omakase sets at standing bars offer great value (¥2,000–¥3,500)

day_by_day.notes: Tsukiji Outer Market is best visited early (8:00–10:00 AM) before it gets crowded. The inner wholesale market has moved to Toyosu, but the outer market remains vibrant. Bring cash — many stalls are cash only.

day_by_day.morning: Explore Ueno Park and its surroundings. Visit the Tokyo National Museum (Japan's largest museum covering Japanese art and antiquities) for a deep cultural dive. Stroll through Ueno Park, check the pond area, and visit Ueno Tosho-gu Shrine within the park.
day_by_day.afternoon: Walk from Ueno to Yanaka — one of Tokyo's best-preserved old shitamachi (downtown) neighborhoods. Wander through Yanaka Ginza shopping street, browse vintage shops, local bakeries, and traditional craft stores. Visit Yanaka Cemetery for its serene, historical atmosphere.
day_by_day.evening: Head to Akihabara (just a short subway ride from Ueno) for an evening preview. Browse the brightly lit electronics and anime shops, grab dinner in the area, and soak in the neon-lit atmosphere.

meals.breakfast: Café or bakery near the hotel or in Ueno — try a morning pastry and coffee at a local café (¥500–¥900)
meals.lunch: Yanaka Ginza street food — try menchi katsu (fried minced meat cutlet), croquettes, or a local café set lunch (¥800–¥1,500)
meals.dinner: Akihabara — try a themed café for the experience (maid café for cultural novelty, budget ¥1,500–¥2,000) or a standard ramen/curry shop in the district (¥900–¥1,500)

day_by_day.notes: Tokyo National Museum is closed on Mondays. Saturday means Akihabara will be lively and busy. Yanaka is a peaceful contrast to the busy tech district — enjoy the slower pace before the evening energy of Akihabara.

day_by_day.morning: Full Akihabara Tech and Anime District Deep Dive. Spend the morning exploring multi-floor electronics shops (Yodobashi Camera, BIC Camera), retro game shops (Super Potato), Gundam model stores, and manga/anime merchandise floors. Visit the Radio Kaikan building for specialty collector shops.
day_by_day.afternoon: Take the subway to Odaiba — Tokyo's futuristic artificial island. Visit teamLab Planets or teamLab Borderless (book tickets in advance) for an immersive digital art experience that blends tech culture and art perfectly. Explore DiverCity Tokyo and see the life-size Unicorn Gundam statue outside.
day_by_day.evening: Enjoy the Odaiba waterfront at sunset with views of Rainbow Bridge and the Tokyo skyline. Dine at a restaurant in the Aqua City or DiverCity mall before heading back.

meals.breakfast: Konbini breakfast or a quick café near Akihabara station before diving in (¥400–¥800)
meals.lunch: Akihabara — try a curry rice shop (Japanese curry is a staple here) or a don (rice bowl) restaurant (¥900–¥1,400)
meals.dinner: Odaiba — mid-range restaurant with a waterfront view. Try a Japanese family restaurant chain like Denny's Japan or a ramen/sushi spot in Aqua City mall (¥1,500–¥2,500)

day_by_day.notes: Book teamLab tickets well in advance online — they frequently sell out, especially on weekends. Odaiba is about 30–40 minutes from Akihabara by subway/Yurikamome line. The Yurikamome monorail ride itself offers great city views.

day_by_day.morning: Visit Harajuku — start at Meiji Jingu (Meiji Shrine), a serene forested Shinto shrine dedicated to Emperor Meiji. Walk the wooded approach path for a peaceful, spiritual experience. This is a beautiful cultural contrast to the busy city.
day_by_day.afternoon: Walk down Takeshita Street in Harajuku for quirky youth fashion, crepe shops, and pop culture stores. Then transition to the nearby Omotesando — Tokyo's tree-lined luxury boulevard. Browse the flagship architecture stores (the Prada building, Omotesando Hills) and visit the Omotesando Hills mall for mid-range shopping.
day_by_day.evening: Head to Shibuya for the iconic Shibuya Crossing experience at night. Visit the Shibuya Sky observation deck (book in advance) for panoramic night views of Tokyo. Explore Shibuya's Center-gai shopping street.

meals.breakfast: Harajuku — try a fresh crepe from Marion Crêpes or Angel Heart on Takeshita Street (¥600–¥900) or a café breakfast near Meiji Shrine
meals.lunch: Omotesando — grab lunch at a stylish café or restaurant in Omotesando Hills. Try Japanese pasta or a café set lunch (¥1,200–¥2,000)
meals.dinner: Shibuya — try a yakiniku (Japanese BBQ) restaurant for a fun dinner experience. Mid-range yakiniku sets run ¥2,500–¥4,000 per person with drinks

day_by_day.notes: Meiji Shrine is open from sunrise to sunset — arrive early for a peaceful experience before crowds. Shibuya Crossing is most dramatic in the evening rush hour (around 6–8 PM). Book Shibuya Sky tickets online in advance.

day_by_day.morning: Day trip to Nikko (about 2 hours from Tokyo by Tobu Nikko Line or Shinkansen connection). Visit the UNESCO World Heritage Tosho-gu Shrine complex — one of Japan's most ornate and historically significant shrine complexes, set in a cedar forest in the mountains.
day_by_day.afternoon: Continue exploring Nikko — visit Rinnoji Temple, Futarasan Shrine, and the Shinkyo Sacred Bridge over the Daiya River. If time allows, take a bus to Kegon Falls, one of Japan's most celebrated waterfalls.
day_by_day.evening: Return to Tokyo by early evening. Arrive back around 7–8 PM. Take a relaxed evening near your hotel neighborhood — explore a local shotengai (covered shopping street) or simply rest.

meals.breakfast: Early breakfast at the hotel or a quick konbini meal before catching the train to Nikko (¥400–¥800)
meals.lunch: Nikko — try yuba (tofu skin) cuisine, a Nikko specialty, at a local restaurant near the shrine complex. Set lunches available (¥1,200–¥2,000)
meals.dinner: Back in Tokyo — casual neighborhood restaurant or ramen shop near the hotel (¥900–¥1,500)

day_by_day.notes: Purchase the Nikko Pass for unlimited Tobu line rides and local bus access — it offers good value. Start early to maximize time in Nikko. The Tosho-gu complex requires an entrance fee (¥1,300). Nikko can be crowded on weekends — a Tuesday visit is ideal.

day_by_day.morning: Visit Shinjuku Gyoen National Garden — one of Tokyo's most beautiful parks, especially stunning in April with late cherry blossoms and spring flowers. Spend a relaxed morning strolling through Japanese, French, and English garden sections.
day_by_day.afternoon: Explore East Shinjuku — visit the Kabukicho entertainment district in daylight, then head to the Tokyo Metropolitan Government Building for free panoramic views from the 45th-floor observation deck. Browse the Takashimaya Times Square department store.
day_by_day.evening: Experience the Ramen Alley Tasting Experience in Shinjuku. Navigate the narrow, atmospheric lanes of Omoide Yokocho (Memory Lane) — a tiny alley of smoky yakitori stalls dating back to the 1940s. Then explore nearby ramen shops for a full evening of Shinjuku's legendary food culture.

meals.breakfast: Café near the hotel or in Shinjuku before the garden opens — try a kissaten (old-school Japanese café) for toast, egg, and coffee (¥600–¥1,000)
meals.lunch: Shinjuku — try a katsu sandwich from a depachika (department store basement food hall) or a tonkatsu restaurant for a classic pork cutlet set (¥1,000–¥1,800)
meals.dinner: Omoide Yokocho — graze on yakitori skewers (chicken, offal, vegetables) and cold beer at the tiny stalls. Budget ¥2,000–¥3,000 for a full evening of eating and drinking. Follow up with a bowl of ramen at a nearby shop if still hungry (¥900–¥1,200)

day_by_day.notes: Shinjuku Gyoen has a small entrance fee (¥500) and is closed Mondays. Alcohol is not permitted in the garden. Omoide Yokocho is tiny and atmospheric — arrive by 7 PM to secure a stool at one of the stalls. The Tokyo Metropolitan Government Building observation is free and open until 10:30 PM on most nights.

day_by_day.morning: Visit Tsukishima neighborhood — famous for monjayaki (Tokyo's savory pancake), this old shitamachi island district is a cultural gem. Stroll the Monja Street and explore the charming old Tokyo atmosphere. Then visit the nearby Kiyosumi-Shirakawa area, known for specialty coffee culture.
day_by_day.afternoon: Head to Koto City's Museum of Contemporary Art Tokyo (MOT) for a world-class contemporary art experience. The museum features rotating international and Japanese exhibitions in a beautiful building. Alternatively, visit the nearby Fukagawa Edo Museum for a reconstructed Edo-period townscape.
day_by_day.evening: Head to Roppongi for the evening — visit the Mori Art Museum (open until 10 PM) on the 53rd floor of Roppongi Hills, which combines contemporary art with sweeping city views. Explore Roppongi's international dining and nightlife scene.

meals.breakfast: Kiyosumi-Shirakawa — visit a specialty third-wave coffee café (Allpress Espresso or Arise Coffee) for excellent pour-over coffee and light breakfast (¥800–¥1,200)
meals.lunch: Tsukishima — eat monjayaki at one of the traditional restaurants on Monja Street. A set with drinks runs ¥1,500–¥2,500
meals.dinner: Roppongi — try a mid-range Japanese restaurant in Roppongi Hills. Options include Japanese shabu-shabu hot pot or a set dinner at a teppanyaki restaurant (¥2,500–¥4,000)

day_by_day.notes: Museum of Contemporary Art Tokyo is closed on Mondays and Tuesdays. Mori Art Museum tickets include the Tokyo City View observation deck — great value. Roppongi has a vibrant nightlife scene if you want to extend the evening.

day_by_day.morning: Visit Ikebukuro — explore the Sunshine City complex, including the Sunshine Aquarium on the rooftop and the Pokemon Center Mega Tokyo (a must for pop culture fans). Explore the Animate flagship store (Japan's largest anime merchandise store).
day_by_day.afternoon: Head to Sugamo — known as 'Grandma's Harajuku,' this traditional shotengai (shopping street) offers a glimpse of old Tokyo life, traditional sweets, and local shops. Visit Koganji Temple and browse the unique red underwear shops (a local specialty said to bring health). Then visit the nearby Komagome area and Rikugien Garden — a stunning traditional Japanese garden.
day_by_day.evening: Return to your hotel area or explore a local neighborhood. Visit a neighborhood sento (public bath house) for an authentic Tokyo cultural experience — a perfect way to relax mid-trip.

meals.breakfast: Ikebukuro — try a bakery breakfast at one of the many shops near the station, or a café morning set (¥600–¥1,000)
meals.lunch: Ikebukuro — the area has excellent Chinese food (large Chinese community nearby). Try a Chinese-Japanese fusion restaurant or a ramen shop (¥900–¥1,500)
meals.dinner: Local neighborhood near your hotel — explore a nearby izakaya or try a gyoza specialty restaurant. Gyoza sets with beer are a great mid-range option (¥1,500–¥2,500)

day_by_day.notes: Rikugien Garden is particularly beautiful in spring — check for any evening illumination events (sometimes held in April). The sento experience typically costs ¥500–¥800 — bring a small towel or rent one. This is a more relaxed day to balance the busy schedule.

day_by_day.morning: Visit Shimokitazawa — Tokyo's bohemian neighborhood beloved for vintage clothing shops, independent cafés, live music venues, and a creative, artsy atmosphere. Spend the morning browsing vintage stores and exploring the maze-like streets.
day_by_day.afternoon: Head to Daikanyama and Nakameguro — two of Tokyo's most stylish neighborhoods. Visit the iconic Daikanyama T-Site (a beautifully designed bookstore and lifestyle complex). Walk along the Meguro River canal (lined with cherry trees — late blooms may still be visible in mid-April). Browse the boutique shops and independent cafés.
day_by_day.evening: Stay in Nakameguro for dinner — the area transforms beautifully at night with warm-lit restaurants along the canal. This is one of Tokyo's most romantic and atmospheric evening dining spots.

meals.breakfast: Shimokitazawa — try a specialty coffee shop or a café brunch with avocado toast or Japanese-style eggs. Many excellent independent cafés in the area (¥800–¥1,400)
meals.lunch: Daikanyama — try a light lunch at the Log Road Daikanyama complex or a bento from the T-Site area. Various international and Japanese options (¥1,200–¥2,000)
meals.dinner: Nakameguro canal — book a table at a mid-range Japanese restaurant along the river. Try a seafood izakaya or a modern Japanese bistro. The atmosphere is exceptional at night (¥2,500–¥4,000)

day_by_day.notes: Saturday in Shimokitazawa is lively — vintage shops are busiest in the afternoon, so morning is ideal. The Meguro River canal walk between Nakameguro and Daikanyama is only about 20 minutes on foot. This is a great day for photography.

day_by_day.morning: Visit the teamLab Planets or Tokyo National Museum (if not yet visited) for a final cultural morning. Alternatively, explore the Koenji neighborhood — known for its alternative culture, vintage shops, and local festivals. Visit Koenji's covered shopping arcades and browse independent record shops and vintage clothing.
day_by_day.afternoon: Head to Akihabara for any last-minute tech or anime shopping (pick up souvenirs, figures, electronics). Then visit the nearby Ochanomizu area — browse the famous musical instrument shops along Ochanomizu's instrument street, and visit the Nikolai Cathedral (an impressive Russian Orthodox cathedral in the heart of Tokyo).
day_by_day.evening: Final evening in Tokyo — head to a rooftop bar or observation deck for a farewell view of the city. Consider the Park Hyatt New York Bar (made famous by Lost in Translation) in Shinjuku for a splurge cocktail, or the free Tokyo Metropolitan Government Building observation deck for budget-friendly night views.

meals.breakfast: Koenji — local neighborhood café or bakery (¥600–¥1,000)
meals.lunch: Akihabara/Ochanomizu — try a curry rice restaurant (Japanese curry is comforting and affordable) or a ramen shop (¥900–¥1,500)
meals.dinner: Farewell dinner — treat yourself to a slightly elevated meal. Try a teppanyaki set dinner, a kaiseki-lite restaurant, or a high-quality sushi counter in Shinjuku or Ginza. Budget ¥4,000–¥7,000 for a memorable final dinner

day_by_day.notes: Use this day for any final souvenir shopping and revisiting favorite spots. Pack any purchases carefully — Japanese department stores offer excellent gift wrapping and tax-free shopping for purchases over ¥5,000. Confirm your departure logistics for tomorrow.

day_by_day.morning: Final morning in Tokyo — wake up early for a peaceful last walk through a nearby park or along a local street. Visit a neighborhood shrine for a quiet morning reflection. Grab a final konbini breakfast or a café morning set — savor the last moments of Tokyo daily life.
day_by_day.afternoon: Check out of the hotel (standard checkout is 11:00 AM — request late checkout if needed). Store luggage at the hotel or at a coin locker at the nearest major train station. Spend your final hours doing any last-minute shopping at a nearby convenience store or department store for omiyage (souvenirs/gifts). Head to the airport with plenty of time — allow 90–120 minutes for the journey plus check-in.
day_by_day.evening: Depart from Tokyo. Browse the airport's extensive duty-free shops and grab a final bowl of ramen or soba at an airport restaurant before your flight. Safe travels!

meals.breakfast: Final neighborhood breakfast — try a traditional Japanese breakfast set one last time at a local café (¥700–¥1,200)
meals.lunch: Near the hotel or airport area — light meal before departure. A bento from a depachika or a quick ramen (¥900–¥1,500)
meals.dinner: Airport restaurant — Narita and Haneda both have excellent dining options including sushi, ramen, tempura, and tonkatsu. Budget ¥1,500–¥2,500 for a proper farewell meal

day_by_day.notes: Narita Airport is 60–90 minutes from central Tokyo; Haneda is 30–45 minutes. Always allow extra time for check-in and security. Return your Suica/Pasmo card at the airport for a refund of the deposit (¥500) and remaining balance. Japan is cash-heavy — spend remaining yen at the airport or convert back before departing.

highlights: Mix of paid and free experiences

trip_options.title: Premium Tokyo, Japan Escape
trip_options.description: Indulge in the best the destination has to offer. Premium flights, luxury hotels, and exclusive experiences.

experiences.name: Tsukiji Outer Market Food Tour
experiences.description: Explore the bustling Tsukiji Outer Market, sampling fresh sushi, tamagoyaki, grilled seafood skewers, and matcha treats from legendary local vendors. Engage with vendors who have operated stalls for generations and experience the authentic culinary heartbeat of Tokyo.

experiences.name: Akihabara Tech and Anime District Deep Dive
experiences.description: Immerse yourself in Tokyo's iconic electric town, visiting multi-floor electronics shops, retro game arcades, maid cafes, and cutting-edge gadget stores. Discover the intersection of consumer tech, gaming culture, and otaku subculture that defines modern Japanese innovation.

experiences.name: Senso-ji Temple and Asakusa Cultural Walk
experiences.description: Visit Tokyo's oldest and most iconic Buddhist temple, Senso-ji, strolling through the Nakamise shopping street lined with traditional crafts and snacks. Witness morning prayers, explore the five-story pagoda, and absorb the Edo-period atmosphere of the surrounding Asakusa district.

experiences.name: Ramen Alley Tasting Experience in Shinjuku
experiences.description: Navigate the narrow, atmospheric lanes of Shinjuku's Omoide Yokocho (Memory Lane) and nearby ramen shops, tasting regional ramen styles from tonkotsu to miso. Join a guided tasting session or self-explore izakayas and ramen counters for an authentic after-dark Tokyo dining ritual.

experiences.name: teamLab Borderless Digital Art Museum
experiences.description: Experience one of the world's most celebrated digital art installations where technology and culture merge into breathtaking immersive environments. Walk through rooms of interactive light, sound, and projection art created by the pioneering art collective teamLab, blending Japanese aesthetics with futuristic innovation.

day_by_day.morning: No activities scheduled — late night arrival. Flight UA lands at 22:30. Private luxury transfer from Narita/Haneda Airport to Aegean Bliss Resort arranged in advance. A dedicated meet-and-greet concierge service will be waiting at the arrivals hall.
day_by_day.afternoon: No activities scheduled — travel day.
day_by_day.evening: Late-night arrival and hotel check-in. Enjoy a welcome amenity prepared by the resort — expect chilled sake, seasonal wagashi (Japanese sweets), and a personalized note from the concierge. Wind down with a relaxing soak in the in-room onsen-style bath if available, or visit the hotel's 24-hour lounge for a light nightcap.

meals.breakfast: Not applicable — travel day.
meals.lunch: Not applicable — in-flight or in transit.
meals.dinner: Light late-night room service at the hotel — recommend ordering the Japanese bento set or a comforting bowl of miso ramen from the in-room dining menu to ease into Tokyo cuisine.

day_by_day.notes: Ensure your hotel concierge is pre-informed of your late arrival. Request a late check-out or flexible morning to recover from jet lag. Keep the first full day light to allow for rest.

day_by_day.morning: Slow, restorative morning at the hotel. Enjoy a leisurely Japanese-Western fusion breakfast at the hotel's signature restaurant. Afterward, take a gentle orientation stroll around the immediate neighborhood to get your bearings — visit a nearby konbini (convenience store) like 7-Eleven or Lawson for a quintessential Tokyo experience, picking up a canned coffee or onigiri.
day_by_day.afternoon: Head to teamLab Borderless Digital Art Museum — a world-renowned immersive digital art experience where technology and nature blur into one breathtaking environment. Book a premium time-slot entry in advance. Spend 2–3 hours wandering through the luminous, ever-changing installations. This experience perfectly blends Tokyo's tech culture with artistic expression.
day_by_day.evening: Dinner in the Odaiba or Azabudai Hills area near teamLab. Reserve a table at a high-end contemporary Japanese restaurant such as Inua or a kaiseki establishment. Return to the hotel by private car or taxi for a restful evening.

meals.breakfast: Hotel breakfast — opt for the Japanese set with grilled fish, tamagoyaki, miso soup, pickles, and steamed rice.
meals.lunch: Light café lunch near teamLab Borderless — try the in-venue café for artistically plated seasonal dishes, or visit a nearby upscale food hall.
meals.dinner: Kaiseki dinner at a refined Tokyo restaurant — recommend Azabudai Hills' curated dining floor featuring seasonal tasting menus. Budget ¥20,000–¥35,000 per person.

day_by_day.notes: teamLab Borderless tickets sell out weeks in advance — confirm booking before departure. Wear comfortable shoes as you'll be walking on uneven, immersive floor surfaces. April weather in Tokyo is mild (12–20°C), so a light jacket is recommended for evenings.

day_by_day.morning: Tsukiji Outer Market Food Tour — join a premium guided tour of the iconic Tsukiji Outer Market. Sample freshly cut sushi, golden tamagoyaki, grilled scallops, sea urchin on rice, and seasonal Japanese street food. A knowledgeable guide will walk you through the history of the market and introduce you to top vendors. Start early (around 8:00 AM) to experience the market at its most vibrant.
day_by_day.afternoon: After the market, head to the nearby Ginza district — Tokyo's most prestigious shopping and cultural quarter. Explore flagship stores of luxury Japanese brands such as Mikimoto, Issey Miyake, and Comme des Garçons. Visit the Itoya stationery flagship store for exquisite Japanese paper goods. Optionally, stop into the Ginza Six luxury mall for curated boutiques and a rooftop garden.
day_by_day.evening: Dinner at a world-class sushi omakase restaurant in Ginza — this neighborhood is home to several Michelin-starred sushi counters. Recommended: Sushi Yoshitake or Sushi Saito (reservation required months in advance). Experience the intimate 10–12 course omakase format with the chef preparing each piece directly in front of you.

meals.breakfast: Tsukiji Outer Market itself IS the breakfast — fresh tuna sashimi, tamagoyaki, oysters, and matcha soft-serve from market stalls.
meals.lunch: Upscale lunch at Ginza's Kyubey sushi restaurant or the premium food hall at Ginza Six — try seasonal chirashi don or a refined bento.
meals.dinner: Michelin-starred omakase sushi dinner in Ginza. Budget ¥30,000–¥60,000 per person. Dress code is smart casual to formal.

day_by_day.notes: Tsukiji Outer Market is open daily but some vendors close on Wednesdays. Arrive before 9:00 AM for the best selection. Sushi omakase restaurants require reservations far in advance — use the hotel concierge to assist with bookings.

day_by_day.morning: Senso-ji Temple and Asakusa Cultural Walk — travel to Asakusa, Tokyo's most atmospheric old-town district. Begin at Senso-ji, Tokyo's oldest Buddhist temple, arriving early (before 9:00 AM) to enjoy the grounds before crowds build. Walk the iconic Nakamise Shopping Street for traditional crafts, fans, and sweets. Explore the backstreets of Yanaka nearby for a glimpse of old Tokyo.
day_by_day.afternoon: Visit the Tokyo National Museum in Ueno Park — the largest art museum in Japan, housing an extraordinary collection of samurai armor, Buddhist sculpture, ukiyo-e woodblock prints, and ancient ceramics. Consider booking a private guided tour for a deeper cultural context. Stroll through Ueno Park, which should be in late cherry blossom or fresh green foliage in mid-April.
day_by_day.evening: Return to the Asakusa area for dinner. Dine at Komagata Dojo, a historic restaurant serving dojo (loach) hotpot that has been operating since 1801, or opt for a premium tempura dinner at Daikokuya Tempura, one of Tokyo's most celebrated tempura establishments. Afterward, take a relaxing rickshaw (jinrikisha) ride through the illuminated Asakusa streets.

meals.breakfast: Hotel breakfast or a traditional Japanese morning set at a local Asakusa café near the temple.
meals.lunch: Lunch at Ueno's upscale Izu-ei restaurant — famous for premium unaju (grilled eel over rice), a Tokyo delicacy. Budget ¥5,000–¥8,000 per person.
meals.dinner: Tempura kaiseki dinner at Daikokuya or a refined Asakusa restaurant. Budget ¥15,000–¥25,000 per person.

day_by_day.notes: Senso-ji is free to enter and open 24 hours, though the inner hall has set hours. April is peak tourist season — arriving before 8:30 AM ensures a more peaceful experience. The rickshaw rides (jinrikisha) can be booked on-site in Asakusa for approximately ¥3,000–¥10,000 depending on route.

day_by_day.morning: Akihabara Tech and Anime District Deep Dive — spend the morning in Tokyo's legendary Electric Town. Explore multi-floor electronics megastores like Yodobashi Akiba and BIC Camera for the latest Japanese tech gadgets, audio equipment, and robotics. Visit retro game shops for rare Famicom cartridges and arcade memorabilia. Explore the famous multi-story arcades for an authentic gaming culture experience.
day_by_day.afternoon: Continue in Akihabara — visit Gundam Café and the AKB48 Theater area for pop culture immersion. Head to the Robot Restaurant area or book a tour of a cutting-edge tech showroom. Alternatively, travel to the nearby Kanda district to explore Jimbocho, Tokyo's famous secondhand bookstore district, for rare Japanese art books and manga collections.
day_by_day.evening: Dinner in the Marunouchi or Nihonbashi area — both are elegant, upscale districts near Akihabara. Dine at a premium teppanyaki restaurant such as Ukai-tei, where master chefs prepare Wagyu beef and seasonal vegetables on a gleaming iron griddle before you. Pair with a curated Japanese whisky flight.

meals.breakfast: Hotel breakfast or a morning set at a Akihabara café — try the themed maid cafés for a cultural curiosity (Cure Maid Café is the most refined option).
meals.lunch: Lunch at a high-end ramen specialty restaurant in Akihabara — try Fuunji for tsukemen (dipping ramen) or a premium tonkotsu counter.
meals.dinner: Teppanyaki Wagyu dinner at Ukai-tei Ginza or Nihonbashi area. Budget ¥25,000–¥45,000 per person. Reserve in advance.

day_by_day.notes: Akihabara is best explored on foot — the main strip and side streets are all walkable. Many electronics stores open at 10:00 AM. If interested in purchasing electronics, confirm voltage compatibility and international warranty coverage before buying.

day_by_day.morning: Private tea ceremony experience — arrange a premium private tea ceremony session in a traditional machiya (townhouse) setting in Yanaka or Omotesando. A certified tea master will guide you through the ritual of matcha preparation, the philosophy of wabi-sabi, and the art of Japanese ceramics. This intimate 90-minute session is a profound cultural highlight.
day_by_day.afternoon: Explore Omotesando — Tokyo's most architecturally stunning boulevard, lined with flagship buildings designed by world-renowned architects (Tadao Ando's Omotesando Hills, Herzog & de Meuron's Prada building). Browse luxury boutiques and Japanese designer concept stores. Visit the Nezu Museum nearby for a serene collection of Asian art and a stunning bamboo garden.
day_by_day.evening: Ramen Alley Tasting Experience in Shinjuku — navigate the atmospheric, lantern-lit lanes of Omoide Yokocho (Memory Lane) in Shinjuku for yakitori skewers and cold Sapporo beer at tiny counter-seat stalls. Follow with a premium ramen tasting at one of Shinjuku's top ramen establishments — try Fuunji or Ichiran for a solo booth experience. Cap the evening with drinks at a high-altitude bar in a Shinjuku skyscraper.

meals.breakfast: Hotel breakfast — Japanese set with seasonal pickles and grilled fish.
meals.lunch: Lunch at Omotesando Hills' curated restaurant floor — try a refined Japanese pasta or seasonal bento from a premium café.
meals.dinner: Omoide Yokocho yakitori stalls for atmosphere and snacks, followed by a signature ramen bowl at a top Shinjuku ramen shop. End with cocktails at the Park Hyatt Tokyo's New York Bar (famous from Lost in Translation). Budget ¥10,000–¥15,000 for the full evening.

day_by_day.notes: The Nezu Museum is closed on Mondays — check the calendar. Omoide Yokocho stalls are tiny and smoky — embrace the atmosphere. The Park Hyatt New York Bar has a ¥2,200 cover charge after 8:00 PM on weekends but the views over Tokyo are extraordinary.

day_by_day.morning: Day trip to Nikko — depart early by private car or the Tobu Nikko Limited Express train (approximately 2 hours). Nikko is a UNESCO World Heritage Site featuring the magnificent Tosho-gu Shrine complex, ornately decorated with gold leaf and intricate wood carvings set against a cedar forest backdrop. Explore the shrine, Rinno-ji Temple, and the sacred Shinkyo Bridge.
day_by_day.afternoon: Continue exploring Nikko — visit the serene Kegon Falls (one of Japan's top three waterfalls) and the peaceful shores of Lake Chuzenji. If time permits, relax at a traditional onsen ryokan in the area for a brief afternoon soak. Begin the return journey to Tokyo by late afternoon.
day_by_day.evening: Return to Tokyo by early evening. Enjoy a quiet dinner near the hotel — opt for a premium izakaya experience at a refined establishment, ordering seasonal small plates: grilled wagyu skewers, sashimi, dashimaki tamago, and cold tofu with yuzu. Pair with premium nihonshu (sake) selected by the sommelier.

meals.breakfast: Early hotel breakfast before departure — or a bento box prepared by the hotel for the train journey.
meals.lunch: Traditional kaiseki lunch at a Nikko ryokan restaurant — seasonal mountain vegetables (sansai), river fish, and tofu dishes. Budget ¥8,000–¥15,000 per person.
meals.dinner: Premium izakaya dinner near the hotel. Recommend Torishiki (yakitori) or a refined sake bar with seasonal small plates. Budget ¥12,000–¥20,000 per person.

day_by_day.notes: Nikko is approximately 150 km from Tokyo. The Tobu Nikko Limited Express (Spacia) is comfortable and scenic — book reserved seats in advance. Tosho-gu Shrine entry is ¥1,300 per person. April foliage in Nikko is stunning — fresh green leaves and lingering cherry blossoms at lower elevations.

day_by_day.morning: Private cooking class with a professional Japanese chef — learn to prepare a multi-course Japanese meal including dashi broth from scratch, miso soup, hand-rolled sushi, and a seasonal side dish. Classes are held in a traditional kitchen setting in central Tokyo. This 3-hour immersive experience connects food culture with hands-on technique.
day_by_day.afternoon: Visit the Mori Art Museum in Roppongi Hills — one of Tokyo's premier contemporary art institutions, often featuring boundary-pushing international and Japanese artists. After the museum, explore the Roppongi Hills complex, including the rooftop Sky Deck with panoramic Tokyo views. Browse the curated art bookshop and design stores.
day_by_day.evening: Dinner in Roppongi — this district is home to some of Tokyo's most internationally acclaimed restaurants. Reserve a table at Ryugin (three Michelin stars), where chef Seiji Yamamoto reinterprets traditional Japanese cuisine through a modern, technically brilliant lens. The tasting menu is a 10+ course journey through Japan's seasons.

meals.breakfast: Hotel breakfast.
meals.lunch: Eat the dishes you prepared in your cooking class — this is the meal! Enjoy a communal lunch with your chef instructor.
meals.dinner: Three Michelin-star kaiseki at Nihon Ryori Ryugin, Roppongi. Budget ¥35,000–¥55,000 per person. Reservations essential — book months ahead via the hotel concierge.

day_by_day.notes: Private cooking classes in Tokyo range from ¥15,000–¥30,000 per person for premium experiences. Confirm dietary restrictions in advance. Ryugin requires formal attire — smart dress or jacket recommended.

day_by_day.morning: Explore the Yanaka and Nezu neighborhoods — one of Tokyo's best-preserved historic districts that survived WWII bombing. Wander the narrow streets, browse independent craft shops, visit the Yanaka Cemetery (peaceful and atmospheric with old cherry trees), and stop into a traditional sembei (rice cracker) bakery. This is Tokyo at its most authentic and unhurried.
day_by_day.afternoon: Visit the Intermediatheque — a cutting-edge museum inside the KITTE building near Tokyo Station, jointly operated by the University of Tokyo and Japan Post. It houses a fascinating collection of natural history specimens, scientific instruments, and art objects displayed in an avant-garde setting. Afterward, explore the KITTE building's stunning atrium and its curated Japanese brand shops.
day_by_day.evening: Tokyo Tower visit at dusk — take a private elevator to the Main Deck and Top Deck for sweeping views of the city as it transitions from golden hour to the glittering nightscape. Follow with dinner at a refined French-Japanese fusion restaurant in the Shiba or Azabudai area nearby.

meals.breakfast: Breakfast at a traditional Yanaka kissaten (old-style Japanese coffee shop) — enjoy a morning set with thick toast, soft-boiled egg, and drip coffee.
meals.lunch: Lunch at KITTE building's restaurant floor — try Marunouchi House for a curated selection of Tokyo's top restaurant brands in a stylish open-air setting.
meals.dinner: French-Japanese fusion dinner near Tokyo Tower — recommend Azabudai Hills' Joel Robuchon Tokyo or a refined contemporary French restaurant. Budget ¥25,000–¥40,000 per person.

day_by_day.notes: Yanaka is best explored on foot with no fixed agenda — allow yourself to get pleasantly lost. The Intermediatheque is free to enter. Tokyo Tower's Top Deck tickets are ¥3,000 per person — book online to avoid queues.

day_by_day.morning: Harajuku and Meiji Shrine — begin the morning at the tranquil Meiji Jingu Shrine, set within a 70-hectare forested park in the heart of Tokyo. The forested approach along the gravel path is meditative and beautiful. Participate in a traditional prayer ritual or simply absorb the serene atmosphere. Afterward, explore the adjacent Yoyogi Park for a leisurely stroll.
day_by_day.afternoon: Explore Harajuku's Takeshita Street for Tokyo's most eccentric street fashion and crepe culture, then transition to the sophisticated Cat Street and Ura-Harajuku for independent designer boutiques and concept stores. Visit Dover Street Market Ginza or the Comme des Garçons flagship. End the afternoon at the Prada Aoyama building for its stunning architecture.
day_by_day.evening: Dinner in Aoyama or Minami-Aoyama — one of Tokyo's most refined dining neighborhoods. Reserve at L'Effervescence (two Michelin stars), where chef Shinobu Namae creates extraordinary French cuisine inspired by Japanese ingredients and philosophy. Alternatively, dine at Florilège for an innovative, vegetable-forward tasting menu.

meals.breakfast: Hotel breakfast or a premium café near Harajuku — try Fuglen Tokyo for specialty Nordic-Japanese coffee and pastries.
meals.lunch: Lunch at a refined Omotesando or Aoyama restaurant — try Anniversaire Café for a garden terrace experience, or a curated Japanese lunch set at Maisen (premium tonkatsu).
meals.dinner: Two Michelin-star dinner at L'Effervescence or Florilège, Minami-Aoyama. Budget ¥30,000–¥50,000 per person. Formal attire required.

day_by_day.notes: Meiji Shrine is free to enter and opens at sunrise. The forested path to the shrine is approximately 800 meters — wear comfortable shoes. Harajuku is liveliest on weekends. April is ideal weather for outdoor strolling in Yoyogi Park.

day_by_day.morning: Day trip to Hakone — depart by Romancecar (Odakyu Limited Express) from Shinjuku Station for a scenic 90-minute journey to Hakone. Check in at a luxury onsen ryokan (recommend Gora Kadan or The Hoshino Resorts KAI Hakone) for a midday arrival. Enjoy a private open-air onsen bath overlooking the mountains — a quintessential Japanese wellness experience.
day_by_day.afternoon: Explore Hakone — visit the Hakone Open Air Museum, one of Japan's finest outdoor sculpture parks featuring works by Picasso, Henry Moore, and Fumio Asakura set against mountain scenery. Take the Hakone Ropeway for aerial views of Mount Fuji (weather permitting in April) and the volcanic Owakudani geothermal valley.
day_by_day.evening: Return to the ryokan for a multi-course kaiseki dinner — a seasonal tasting menu prepared by the ryokan's chef, served in your private room or the main dining hall. Dishes highlight local Hakone ingredients: mountain vegetables, freshwater fish, and regional tofu. Afterward, enjoy a second private onsen soak under the stars.

meals.breakfast: Hotel breakfast in Tokyo before departure.
meals.lunch: Arrival at ryokan — light seasonal lunch or a traditional bento served upon check-in. Alternatively, try the Hakone Open Air Museum café for a scenic lunch.
meals.dinner: Full kaiseki dinner at the ryokan — 8–12 courses of seasonal Japanese cuisine. Included in most luxury ryokan packages. Budget ¥30,000–¥60,000 per person for room and dinner.

day_by_day.notes: This is an overnight stay in Hakone — pack an overnight bag. Luxury ryokan in Hakone require advance reservations (often 2–3 months). Mount Fuji visibility in April is moderate — morning hours offer the best chance of clear views. Yukata (cotton robes) are provided by the ryokan for evening wear.

day_by_day.morning: Wake up early for a private sunrise onsen soak at the ryokan. Enjoy a traditional Japanese breakfast served in your room — grilled fish, tofu, pickled vegetables, tamago, rice, and miso soup. After breakfast, take a morning walk along the Hakone nature trails near the ryokan for fresh mountain air and forest bathing (shinrin-yoku).
day_by_day.afternoon: Return to Tokyo by Romancecar. Upon arrival, head to the Shibuya district — visit the newly opened Shibuya Sky observation deck for a 360-degree aerial view of Tokyo. Explore the Shibuya Stream and Scramble Square complexes. Watch the iconic Shibuya Crossing from above at the Mag's Park observation deck — the world's busiest pedestrian intersection.
day_by_day.evening: Final premium dining experience in Shibuya or Ebisu — reserve a table at Joël Robuchon Tokyo (three Michelin stars) in the Château de Joël Robuchon for an extraordinary French fine dining experience in a stunning mansion setting. Alternatively, dine at Sushi Saito if a reservation was secured. End the evening with craft cocktails at a speakeasy-style bar in Ebisu or Daikanyama.

meals.breakfast: Traditional ryokan breakfast — served in-room, paired with green tea and seasonal pickles.
meals.lunch: Light lunch in Shibuya — try the premium food hall at Shibuya Hikarie or a refined Japanese lunch set at a Daikanyama restaurant.
meals.dinner: Three Michelin-star dinner at Joël Robuchon Tokyo, Ebisu. Budget ¥40,000–¥70,000 per person. Black tie or formal attire expected. Book months in advance.

day_by_day.notes: Shibuya Sky observation deck tickets (¥2,000) should be booked online. The Shibuya Crossing is most spectacular at evening rush hour (6–8 PM). Hakone to Shibuya by Romancecar takes approximately 90 minutes — time your return accordingly.

day_by_day.morning: Final morning in Tokyo — enjoy a leisurely hotel breakfast and take time to pack and prepare for departure. Visit a nearby high-end depachika (department store basement food hall) such as Isetan Shinjuku or Takashimaya for premium Japanese food souvenirs: wagashi, matcha, premium dashi, artisan pickles, and beautifully packaged confections. The depachika experience is itself a cultural highlight.
day_by_day.afternoon: Last afternoon exploration — visit the teamLab Planets (Toyosu) if not yet visited, or revisit a favorite neighborhood for any last-minute shopping. Alternatively, spend a reflective afternoon at the Hamarikyu Gardens — a stunning traditional Japanese garden with a teahouse set against the backdrop of Tokyo's modern skyline. Enjoy a bowl of matcha and wagashi in the garden teahouse.
day_by_day.evening: Farewell dinner at the hotel's signature restaurant or a nearby establishment — keep it elegant but unhurried. Opt for a refined shabu-shabu or sukiyaki dinner where premium Wagyu beef is cooked tableside in delicate broth. After dinner, arrange a private luxury transfer to the airport for your departure flight.

meals.breakfast: Final hotel breakfast — order both Japanese and Western options to savor the last morning.
meals.lunch: Depachika grazing at Isetan Shinjuku basement — assemble a curated selection of premium prepared foods, sushi, and seasonal sweets for a standing lunch experience.
meals.dinner: Farewell shabu-shabu or sukiyaki dinner at a premium establishment such as Seryna (Roppongi) or Imahan (Shinjuku) — Wagyu beef courses with seasonal accompaniments. Budget ¥20,000–¥35,000 per person.

day_by_day.notes: Allow at least 3 hours before your flight for airport transfer and check-in — Tokyo airports are 60–90 minutes from the city center. The hotel concierge can arrange luggage forwarding (takkyubin) directly to the airport the night before for convenience. Purchase any last-minute souvenirs at the airport's premium duty-free — Narita and Haneda both have excellent selections of Japanese whisky, cosmetics, and confections.
